title: Select [IS NULL / IS NOT NULL]
description:
## NULL
NULL means "no value" - not 0, not empty string, just nothing. You can't check for NULL with `=` because NULL isn't equal to anything, not even itself.

```sql
-- WRONG: this doesn't work
SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = NULL;

-- RIGHT: use IS NULL
SELECT * FROM users WHERE name IS NULL;

-- Find rows that DO have a value
SELECT * FROM users WHERE name IS NOT NULL;
```

---
## Assignment:
Some BWS servers were added without a status. Find all servers that are missing a status.
setupCode: CREATE TABLE servers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, cpu_cores INTEGER, status TEXT); INSERT INTO servers VALUES (1, 'prod-1', 8, 'running'), (2, 'prod-2', 16, 'running'), (3, 'staging-1', 4, NULL), (4, 'dev-box', 2, 'on fire'), (5, 'mystery-box', 8, NULL);
expectedOutput:
id | name | cpu_cores | status
3 | staging-1 | 4 |
5 | mystery-box | 8 |
